enonce_markdown: An organism that has two identical alleles for a particular gene is said to be:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The prefix tells the answer: homo- means the same, hetero- means different.

### Solution

Having two identical alleles of a gene (for example TT or tt) is the homozygous condition. Heterozygous organisms (also called hybrids) carry two different alleles. **Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: The physical appearance of an organism for a given characteristic, such as tall or short, is called its:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Genotype is the genetic make-up written with letters; phenotype is what can be seen or measured.

### Solution

The observable feature is the phenotype. The genotype is the combination of alleles carried, an allele is one form of a gene, and a gamete is a sex cell. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: In maize, a plant has the genotype Gg. This plant is described as:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Read the two letters of the genotype: identical letters are homozygous, different letters are heterozygous.

### Solution

Gg contains two different alleles, so the plant is heterozygous (a hybrid). Pure breeding or homozygous genotypes would be GG or gg. **Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown: Different forms of the same gene, for example the alleles for red and white petals, are called:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A gene can exist in alternative versions; each version is an allele.

### Solution

Alternative forms of one gene, found at the same position on a pair of chromosomes, are called alleles. Chromosomes carry many genes, and phenotypes are observable characteristics. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown:
Two pea plants both have purple flowers. One has the genotype PP and the other Pp. (P = purple, dominant; p = white.)

(a) State the phenotype of each plant.

(b) State whether the genotype of each plant is homozygous or heterozygous.

(c) State what the example shows about the difference between genotype and phenotype.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare what is seen (phenotype) with the alleles carried (genotype), and apply the idea of dominance.

### Solution

(a) Both plants have the same phenotype: **purple flowers**.

(b) PP is **homozygous (dominant)**; Pp is **heterozygous**.

(c) Plants with different genotypes can have the same phenotype, because the dominant allele P masks the recessive allele p in Pp. The phenotype is only the visible result of the genotype.

enonce_markdown: Explain why a heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) and a homozygous tall pea plant (TT) look the same but are not genetically identical. In your answer name the gametes that each plant produces.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Dominance affects the phenotype only; the genotype decides which gametes are formed, and so what can be passed on.

### Solution

Tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t), so the dominant allele is expressed in both plants and both are **tall**.

The genotypes differ: TT has two identical alleles, Tt has two different alleles.

- TT produces only one type of gamete: all **T**.
- Tt produces two types of gamete in equal numbers: **T** and **t**.

The Tt plant can therefore pass on the recessive allele and may have dwarf offspring when crossed with another plant carrying t, while the TT plant cannot.
